records.original_english_definition: To a fairly large degree, but not completely.
records.source_supported_observation: The draft fairly-large-degree sense fits gradable long; British quite with non-gradable adjectives can instead mean completely. Unrelated topic CEFR badges must not be used as exact-sense levels.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: အတော်အတန်၊ အတော်လေး (အတိုင်းအတာတစ်ခုအထိ)
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: The journey was quite long, but we enjoyed it.

records.original_english_definition: To a noticeable degree, often more than expected.
records.original_burmese_meaning: အတော်လေး၊ ထင်ထားသည်ထက်ပို၍
records.original_example_sentence: The instructions were rather difficult to follow.
records.source_supported_observation: The draft degree sense is supported; rather can imply surprise, mild criticism or disappointment and is often stronger than quite in British usage. Do not conflate with rather than expressing preference.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: အတော်လေး၊ ထင်ထားသည်ထက်ပို၍ (တစ်ခါတစ်ရံ မနှစ်သက်မှုသဘောပါ)
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: The instructions were rather difficult to follow.

records.original_english_definition: Used to say what is true, especially when it differs from what someone expected.
records.original_burmese_meaning: တကယ်တော့၊ အမှန်တကယ်
records.original_example_sentence: I thought it was Tuesday, but it is actually Wednesday.
records.source_supported_observation: The draft contrasts belief and fact. Actually can politely correct a statement; it does not mean currently or at present. Avoid misleading temporal Myanmar glosses.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: တကယ်တော့၊ အမှန်မှာ (ထင်ထားသည့်အချက်ကို ပြင်ဆင်ဖော်ပြရာတွင်)
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: I thought the meeting was on Tuesday, but it is actually on Wednesday.

records.original_english_definition: Used to introduce a fact that contrasts with what was just said.
records.original_example_sentence: The room was small; however, it was comfortable.
records.source_supported_observation: The draft contrasts clauses and uses a semicolon correctly. However also has a distinct degree sense meaning to whatever extent. A comma splice with however is not equivalent to a conjunction but.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: သို့သော်၊ ဒါပေမဲ့ (ရှေ့ကပြောထားသည့်အချက်နှင့် ဆန့်ကျင်ဘက်ကို ဆက်ပြောရာတွင်)
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: The room was small; however, it was comfortable.

records.original_english_definition: For that reason; as a result.
records.original_example_sentence: The road was closed; therefore, we took another route.
records.source_supported_observation: Therefore introduces a logical consequence, unlike however which signals contrast. The draft semicolon construction is appropriate; avoid treating therefore as a subordinating conjunction.
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: The road was closed; therefore, we took another route.

records.original_english_definition: In the end, after a period of time or several difficulties.
records.original_example_sentence: After several attempts, she eventually solved the problem.
records.source_supported_observation: Eventually marks the end of a period or process, not the last item of a speech or list. Cambridge publisher grammar supports this distinction; Cambridge dictionary indexed B2 conflicts with provisional B1 but direct dictionary page returned 403, so no independently verified CEFR correction.
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: After several attempts, she eventually solved the problem.
